newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks switch back to losses.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks switch back to losses.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed lower Tuesday, weighed down by rising U.S. long bond yields despite a rally on Wall Street, dealers said.

"I think we can blame this fall on new U.S. economic indicators, including wholesale sales growth of 2.1 percent, which show strength in the economy -- now everyone's waiting for retail sales and inflation data due out later in the week," said Jorge Bonanno at brokers Interfin.
The blue-chip MerVal index, which lost 2.3 percent last week and finished flat Monday, retreated 0.8 percent to close at 716.54.
Traders noted the U.S. wholesale sales growth was the strongest since August 1994 and helped drive U.S. long bond yields to 7.11 percent from 7.07 percent at the opening.

"In the next 48 hours we could see yields stretch to 7.19 percent or 7.20 percent, which should spawn more mild sales in our market pushing the MerVal down to between 705 and 711," said Bonanno. "After that, I expect stocks to recover on short-covering ahead of April 23 options expirations, with a MerVal target of 750."
The broad market closed off 0.7 percent, with decliners beating risers 28 to 10 and 20 issues closing unchanged.
Floor volume remained very weak but firmed to 17.8 million pesos from 16.3 million Monday, while over-the-counter deals picked up to 88.4 million pesos from 71.7 million Monday.

Heaviest main-tier losers were textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, which lost 2.2 percent, carmaker Ciadea, down 2.1 percent, and steelmaker Siderca, construction stock Polledo and Banco Frances, all off 1.9 percent.
The only MerVal gainers were oil company Astra and power distributor Central Costanera, both up 0.9 percent, and real estate developer Irsa, up 0.3 percent.
